The test image shows a tomato branch with a dark brown/reddish-brown stem lesion at a node junction, with the entire branch above wilted and dead (brown/black dried leaves still attached). Some pale/white material visible at the stem junction. This is primarily a stem lesion causing branch die-off.

Top candidates: Gray_Mold (stem girdling causing wilt), Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (white mycelium on stem), Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Phytophthora_Blight.

Let me check reference images one at a time.
Gray Mold stem shows a tan/light brown lesion with concentric rings — the test image is much darker (almost black-brown) and more severe. Let me check Sclerotinia.
Sclerotinia shows bleached white stem at soil line with black sclerotia — doesn't match. Let me check Phytophthora Blight stem.
Phytophthora Blight shows very dark blackish stem girdling with total collapse — visually closer to the test image. Let me check Bacterial Canker stem.
Bacterial Canker shows internal stem vascular browning (cut stem) — not matching. Let me check Alternaria Stem Cankers.
Alternaria shows dark canker at soil line with white mycelium at edges. Let me check the other Alternaria reference.
I need to cover more classes. Let me check Late Blight and Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.
Late Blight shows dark leaf patches, not matching the stem pattern. Last view — Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus stem.

Now I have all 8 views. Let me summarize the analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Main green tomato stem with one side branch completely dead at the node junction
- Dead branch stem is very dark reddish-brown to almost black
- White/pale material visible at the node junction where the dead branch meets the main stem
- Leaves on dead branch are dark brown, dried, still attached
- Main plant remains green and healthy

**Reference comparison summary:**
- **Gray_Mold stem**: Tan/light brown concentric lesion girdling stem — color lighter than test, but pattern (node girdling → branch death above) matches perfectly
- **Phytophthora_Blight stem**: Very dark/black stems with complete collapse — best color match, but typically causes whole-plant collapse
- **Sclerotinia stem**: Bleached white at soil line with sclerotia — doesn't match location or color
- **Bacterial_Canker stem**: Internal split-stem view — doesn't match
- **Alternaria stem (Bugwood_4)**: Dark canker at soil junction with white margins — partial match for location/color
- **Alternaria (Bugwood_13)**: Microscopy view — not useful
- **Late_Blight leaf**: Dark leaf patches — doesn't match stem pattern
- **TSWV stem**: Dead side shoot on tomato plant, similar overall structural pattern

**Decision:** The white/pale material at the node junction is consistent with Botrytis spore mass. The single-branch death originating at a node is the classic Gray Mold girdling behavior. While the color is darker than the reference, advanced/dried Botrytis lesions can become very dark. The node attack site and complete wilt above the lesion are the strongest visual indicators.
